record.paper_title: Logical connections between some open problems concerning nil rings
record.original_question: If R is a finitely generated ring, must the radical of R be a nil ideal of R?

evidence.quote: P7 If R is a finitely generated ring, is the radical of R a nil ideal in R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be an associative ring (not assumed to be unital or commutative) that is finitely generated as a ring; that is, there exist finitely many elements $r_1,\dots,r_n \in R$ such that $R$ is the smallest subring of $R$ containing $r_1,\dots,r_n$. Recall that the Jacobson radical $J(R)$ of $R$ is the intersection of all maximal modular right ideals of $R$ (equivalently, the largest ideal $I$ of $R$ such that $1-xy$ has a quasi-inverse for every $x \in I$ and $y \in R$ in the appropriate sense). An ideal $N$ of $R$ is called nil if every element of $N$ is nilpotent.

Question: Must the Jacobson radical $J(R)$ of every finitely generated ring $R$ be a nil ideal of $R$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the Jacobson radical of every finitely generated (associative) ring is nil is a long-standing open problem, closely tied to Amitsur's questions and to the Köthe conjecture. Although Smoktunowicz's example (a nil algebra whose polynomial ring is not nil) settled a related Amitsur conjecture, the problem of whether the radical of an arbitrary finitely generated ring is nil remains open.

status_evidence.title: A polynomial ring that is Jacobson radical and not nil (Smoktunowicz)
status_evidence.snippet: Smoktunowicz constructed an example resolving a related Amitsur conjecture; the question of whether the Jacobson radical of a finitely generated ring must be nil remains an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related conjectures of Amitsur have been studied; the broader question about finitely generated rings is still open.

status_evidence.title: Jacobson radical - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: For a commutative finitely generated algebra over a field or Z, J(R) equals the nilradical, but in the non-commutative finitely generated case this is an open question.
status_evidence.claim: In the non-commutative finitely generated setting, whether J(R) is nil is not known.
